The laws of logarithms are:

- $\log_n(a)+\log_n(b)=\log_n(ab)$ - the product rule

- $\log_n(a)-\log_n(b)=\log_n(\frac{a}{b})$ - the quotient rule

- $\log_n(c^m)=m\log_n(c)$ - the power rule

Note that $\log_{5}\left(x^{2}y^{3}\right)$ can be rewritten using the product and power rules as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\log_{5}\left(x^{2}y^{3}\right) &=\log_{5}\left(x^{2}\right)+\log_{5}\left(y^{3}\right) \\ &=2\log_{5}\left(x\right)+3\log_{5}\left(y\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\log_{5}\left(x\right)=-1$ and $\log_{5}\left(y\right)=-2$, we conclude that

$$
2\log_{5}\left(x\right)+3\log_{5}\left(y\right)=2\cdot (-1)+3\cdot (-2)=-8.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\log_{5}\left(x^{2}y^{3}\right)=-8.
$$
